newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips to pull out of media sector-paper.
newsitem.headline: Philips to pull out of media sector-paper.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Saturday it would gradually wind down its media activities, but would leave its PolyGram stake untouched.
Chairman Cor Boonstra said in an interview with Dutch daily NRC Handelsblad that he thought the Dutch electronics giant was ill-equiped for the fast-moving media sector.
The one exception is its 75 percent stake in music and entertainment group PolyGram, which Boonstra is keen to expand.
"We shall expand with PolyGram, for the rest we will gradually pull out," he told the newspaper.
Boonstra admitted the sector offered interesting possibilities, but said Philips was unable to take full advantage of them.

"We don't have a wonderful track record if you look at our investments in the media sector. It also has to do with our characteristics: We are much better at making products than selling services. The media activities have cost us quite a lot of money."
The complete withdrawl from media activities would be the latest step in a series of moves taken by Boonstra since he took over as chairman from Jan Timmers in October 1996.
Timmers started Philips' Media Division four years ago.
Since taking control, Boonstra has announced his intention to rid the company of what he has called "the bleeders" -- the underperforming and non-core businesses.
Measures already taken include the disposal of home entertainment businesses Videoland and Superclub, and of its cable television interests.
